exposure: Extrapolated Time in Range (eTIR) from SMBG measures
cohort: The study included 140 women with singleton pregnancies and type 1 diabetes who began antenatal care before 20 weeks of gestation and delivered live newborns without malformations between 2010 and 2019.
finding: Higher extrapolated time in range (eTIR) values were associated with a reduced risk of preterm birth, neonatal respiratory distress, and large for gestational age (LGA) infants.
